narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 68.7% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your first-year and third-year class rankings were the strongest influences, both pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. You placed in the bottom decile (1 out of 10) for both Year 1 and Year 3, far below the average of roughly the 6th decile among students who were accepted. These unusually low rankings signaled to the model a higher risk that you would struggle with the bar exam.

Your LSAT score of 38 was the third most important factor and worked in the opposite direction. This score is slightly above the average of 37.2 among accepted students, so it helped pull the prediction toward passing. Unfortunately, this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the negative impact of your class rankings.

Your family income, undergraduate GPA of 3.4, full-time status, gender, and race played little or no role in the outcome.

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance in law school so that your class rank improves significantly. A stronger ranking in the upper half of your class would likely change the model’s prediction and open future opportunities. Consider seeking academic support early and tracking your progress each semester.

Your goal is to generate an explanatory narrative based on the information provided (1-5), explaining why the law school application was denied for this student.

1. DATASET INFORMATION
The dataset contains information on students who took the bar exam.

The target variable is whether the student passed the bar exam on the first try (0 = passed, 1 = failed).

Protected attributes gender and race were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward "will fail" (bar exam failure), negative toward "will pass" (bar exam success). Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

3. STUDENT PROFILE 
You are writing a narrative tailored to this specific person who is rejected law school admission.

- gender = female (the gender of the student.)

- Predicted probability of failure: 68.7%

Feature  SHAP_Value

   lsat   -0.148949

Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
1) The model's predicted probability of bar exam failure and what this means for the student.
